title: creditshelf-tier-brainstorm
content:
Purpose: quick personal notebook for a credit-shelf + slab pricing toy model. Not meant for execs — raw math, hand-wavy assumptions, tradeoffs, and open questions.

Top-level goal: find a simple consumer-friendly front-end (credits) that maps to predictable unit economics for us and feels fair for small teams. Want easy free tier, clear step-ups, and an optional enterprise slab for steady-state volume.

Assumptions (ballpark):
- GPU cost per hour (amortized infra + infra ops + network): $3.00/hr (baseline low-end dedicated/spot mix)
- Avg generation throughput (tokens/sec per GPU): 300 tok/s (varies by model/quantization)
- tokens_per_hour = 300 * 3600 = 1,080,000 tok/hr
- raw_compute_cost_per_token = 3 / 1,080,000 = 2.78e-6 $/tok -> $0.00278 per 1k tokens
- add infra overhead (control plane, storage, padding, rate limiting) ~+40% -> $0.0039 per 1k
- ops margin / business adj ~+60% -> target unit cost to bill ~ $0.01 per 1k tokens (target starting point)

Notes: these numbers change dramatically with batching, cache hits, and sequence length. If we get 2x effective throughput via batching then raw_compute halves -> big impact.

Credit shelf primitives:
- 1 credit = 1k tokens (explicit mapping keeps UX simple)
- Free tier: 100 credits/month (100k tokens) -> covers small tests, demos
- Starter: 10k credits for $10/mo -> $0.001 per 1k (intro price, loss leader)
- Growth: 1M credits for $900/mo -> $0.0009 per 1k (volume discount, encourages commitment)
- Enterprise slab: custom committed price ~ negotiable but baseline $0.0005 per 1k beyond commitment

Rationale: credits simplify per-route metering and cross-model fallbacks. Map credits to tokens (1 credit = 1k tok) to avoid confusion. Provide auto-convert at checkout and show approximate USD cost per credit.

Different pricing levers to expose:
- Per-credit price (obvious)
- Per-model multiplier (higher for Llama2-70B or quality tiers) e.g., model_multiplier 1x/1.5x/3x -> credits consumed scales, keeps front-end simple
- Route multiplier (rerank, embedding heavy calls) -> e.g., embeddings = 0.1 credits per 1k tokens? maybe better to price per-embedding unit instead
- Burst buckets (short term top-ups) vs. monthly committed buckets (auto-renew)

Example user flows and math:
- Developer uses 50k tokens in a month (prototyping): consumes 50 credits -> falls under free (100) => no charge -> good for PLG funnel
- Small app: 2M tokens/mo -> 2000 credits -> under Starter? wait Starter was 10k credits, so they'd pick Starter for $10; this implies huge margins in early pricing. Need to re-evaluate Starter size vs. price.

Adjusting slab sizes (more realistic):
- Starter: 100k credits ($20) -> $0.0002 per 1k -> friendly but closer to cost
- SMB: 1M credits ($150) -> $0.00015 per 1k
- Scale: 10M credits ($1200) -> $0.00012 per 1k

Tradeoffs here: PLG friction if starter too expensive; unsustainable if too cheap. Consider time-limited promos (first 3 months at lower price).

Edge cases:
- Long contexts ( >8k tokens ) disproportionately increases compute cost: consider model-length surcharges or sliding credit multiplier by sequence length band.
- Embeddings: separate unit (e.g., 1 embedding vector = 1 embedding-unit). Keep embeddings outside credit shelf or translate 1 embedding = X credits. This prevents confusion on very long contexts.
- Tooling calls & function calling: often small tokens but many calls -> meter by req-count + tokens to avoid bill shock.

Unit economics sensitivity table (quick):
- If throughput = 600 tok/s (2x): raw_compute per 1k -> $0.0014 -> our target bill per 1k could be $0.005
- If GPU hourly cost = $6: per 1k -> $0.0056 -> billable $0.012+
- Cache hit-rate 30% (prefix): effective per-1k cost decreases proportionally -> big leverage for apps with repeated prefixes

UX details:
- Show "credits remaining" prominently, with approximate USD value tooltip (e.g., 1 credit ≈ $0.01) but allow customers to buy in USD tiers (reduce cognitive load)
- Allow per-route overrides (team-level routing to cheaper model with lower multiplier)
- Expiry: credits expire after 12 months by default; 6 months for promos; enterprise unlimited rollover negotiated

Questions / TODOs:
- How to present model multipliers without scaring non-technical users? (visual badges + "estimated credits per call")
- Do we need separate SKU for embeddings vs generation or keep unified credits? (ask product analytics for 90-day usage split) -> LINK: JIRA-PLT-872
- Investigate bundling with Dedicated offering: commit X credits -> discount + reserved capacity. Align accounting between hosted credits and dedicated commits.
- Build a simple estimator widget in Console that converts average prompt/response lengths to credits and shows monthly cost. High priority for onboarding.

Open decisions (short list):
- Starter slab sizing & pricing (optimize for conversion vs unit-econ)
- Mapping for embeddings and tool-calls
- Model multipliers and how granular they are (broad buckets vs per-model)

Random notes to self: keep one configuration with simpler UX (3 tiers + enterprise) and another with granular credits for power users. Test both in checkout A/B.

End of page (will revisit after metrics from trials and SRE on actual per-model throughput).
